answer: Simultaneous stress probes catch farms that time-share one model. At a random moment each epoch, every seat gets a hard reasoning task at once, sent and timed by a falcon, an established agent drawn at random for that job. Replies must land before the ridge, a latency cutoff set so each seat needs a full model instance of its own. Honest seats show a mesa, a flat plateau in graded quality across the probe; farm seats show a shared quality drop as load spikes, and seats that dip together are merged into one. Each fake needs dedicated compute reserved for that unknown moment, every epoch.
